verses.text: How terrible for Ariel, Ariel, the city where David camped! Add year to year, and let your festivals go on.
Then I will bring trouble on Ariel. There will be mourning and weeping. The city will become to me like an altar hearth, burning with fire.
I will set up camp all around you. I will surround you with towers and build siege works against you.

You will be brought low. You will speak from the ground. Your words will come mumbling out of the dust. Your voice will sound like a ghost coming up from the ground. Your words will whisper out of the dust.
But your many enemies will become like fine dust, and the crowds of cruel attackers like chaff blowing away. It will happen suddenly, in an instant.
The LORD of Armies will come against them with thunder, earthquake, and loud noise, with windstorm and storm, and with flames of a fire that burns everything up.
Then the crowds of all the nations that fight against Ariel, that attack her and her fortress and bring trouble on her, will be like a dream, like a vision in the night.

It will be like a hungry person who dreams they are eating, but wakes up still hungry. It will be like a thirsty person who dreams they are drinking, but wakes up weak and still thirsty. That is how it will be for the crowds of all the nations that fight against Mount Zion.
Be shocked and amazed! Blind yourselves and stay blind! They are drunk, but not from wine. They stagger, but not from strong drink.
For the LORD has poured on you a spirit of deep sleep. He has closed your eyes, you prophets. He has covered your heads, you seers.
This whole vision is like the words of a sealed book to you. If you give it to someone who can read and say, "Please read this," they will answer, "I cannot, because it is sealed."
If you give the book to someone who cannot read and say, "Please read this," they will answer, "I do not know how to read."
The Lord says, "These people come near to me with their mouths and honor me with their lips, but their hearts are far away from me. Their worship of me is made up only of rules taught by people.
So once again I will do amazing things among these people, wonder upon wonder. The wisdom of their wise people will disappear, and the understanding of their clever people will vanish."
How terrible for those who try hard to hide their plans from the LORD, who do their work in the dark and say, "Who sees us? Who will know?"

You turn everything upside down! Is the potter the same as the clay? Can something that was made say about the one who made it, "He did not make me"? Can a pot say about the potter, "He knows nothing"?
In a very short time, Lebanon will be turned into a fruitful field, and the fruitful field will seem like a forest.
On that day the deaf will hear the words of the book, and the eyes of the blind will see out of gloom and darkness.
The humble will be filled with fresh joy in the LORD, and the poorest people will celebrate in the Holy One of Israel.
For the cruel will come to nothing, the mockers will disappear, and all who look for chances to do evil will be cut off,
those who make someone guilty with a word, who set traps for the one who defends justice in court, and who use lies to take away justice from the innocent.
So this is what the LORD, who rescued Abraham, says to the people of Jacob: "Jacob will no longer be ashamed. Their faces will no longer turn pale.
When they see their children, the work of my hands, among them, they will honor my name as holy. They will honor the Holy One of Jacob, and they will stand in awe of the God of Israel.
Those who are confused in spirit will gain understanding, and those who complain will accept teaching."
